newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND MATCHES IN GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Programme of soccer matches in the German first division at the weekend in addition to Saturday's clash between Borussia Dortmund and Borussia Moenchengladbach, Reuters European match of the week (league positions in parentheses, kickoff times GMT):

Stuttgart hitting form with an astonishing 13 goals in their last three games, including 4-1 defeat of leaders Borussia Dortmund. They should be capable of three points at struggling Fortuna, who have lost four of 11 games at home so far.
Bremen's talented Austrian midfielder Andreas Herzog doubtful because of injury but Werder are unbeaten in last four home games. Duisburg need points to get out of relegation danger.
Promoted Bochum are the surprise team of the season but have won just twice away from home. Hamburg have to make changes with defender Andreas Fischer suspended.
Both teams have struggled lately. Cologne need a win to keep alive their UEFA Cup aspirations and St. Pauli are struggling in relegation zone. Cologne without suspended libero Thomas Cichon.
Relegation-threatened Rostock have not won away from home since the sixth day of the season. The fact that 1860 should be at full strength will not help their hopes of ending the poor run.
Schalke on a high after reaching semifinals of UEFA Cup during the week but defender Thomas Linke is suspended and midfielder Tom Dooley on international duty for United States.

Leverkusen have superb chance to keep up the pressure at the top with a game against a weak team who looking almost certain to go down. Bayer are without defender Christian Woerns and Dutch forward Erik Meijer (both suspended). Freiburg have not won for 10 games and six points drift at the bottom.

Bayern recovering from controversy-packed week during which striker Juergen Klinsmann announced he was going to leave at end of season because he is unhappy at the club. Klinsmann is suspended for match because of bookings. Carsten Jancker expected to take his place.
